name: clean-repo
description:
A repository Ghost has scanned and found nothing wrong with is still an asset.

Assets used to be created exclusively inside the findings loop -- get_all_repositories walked and logged every repository, and then repo_map was consulted only when a finding referenced it. A clean codebase was therefore fetched, logged, and discarded, which made this an import of findings grouped by repository rather than an inventory of repositories. Here `spotless-service` has no finding against it at all and must still arrive, carrying its deployment hostnames and no vulnerabilities; `flagged-service` beside it proves the findings path still attaches.

`undeployed-tool` is the deliberate exception. Ghost publishes no addresses -- every mapping hard-codes "ips": [] -- so the deployment hostnames are the only thing tying a repository asset to anything else in the inventory. A repository deployed nowhere would be imported as an orphan that can never merge, so it is skipped, logged, and counted. ids_absent pins that.

namespaced_ids is skipped because the foreign id is the bare repository name with no tenant scope -- a known defect outside the scope of this change.
